summary: Validated Resend email webhook integration end-to-end: single email fires on payment success, idempotent on webhook replay, live status endpoint unaffected, regression suite 23/23 pass.

test_results.webhook_success_triggers_email: PASS (functional) — POST /api/paxity/webhook with SUCCESS payload returned 200 {received:true}; MongoDB orders.ord_ta_email1 updated to status='success' and confirmation_email_sent=true; backend.err.log contains exactly 1 line '[Email] Order confirmation sent for ord_ta_email1 (id=5ad0f532-...)'. One real email was delivered to bafatoumata414@gmail.com.
test_results.idempotence_no_second_email: PASS — 2nd identical webhook POST returned 200; confirmation_email_sent remained true; grep count for '[Email] Order confirmation sent for ord_ta_email1' stays at 1 (atomic find_one_and_update on the flag prevents duplicate sends).
test_results.live_status_endpoint: PASS — GET /api/paxity/status/tx_46be2c7da52a46a6 returned 200 with status='pending' (no crash, live refresh path exercises the new email hook safely).
test_results.regression_suite: PASS — 23/23 tests in test_paxity_parsing.py + test_tracking.py + test_paxity_diagnostic_preview.py

critical_code_review_comments: email_service.maybe_send_order_confirmation correctly uses an atomic find_one_and_update on the confirmation_email_sent flag before calling resend — guarantees exactly-once semantics across concurrent webhook+status-poll races.

On send failure the code releases the flag via a follow-up update; this can theoretically double-send if Resend actually delivered but returned an error. Acceptable tradeoff, but consider logging the resend response body on the exception path for post-mortem visibility.

SENDER_EMAIL defaults to onboarding@resend.dev which restricts recipients to the account owner in Resend test mode — matches current MERCHANT_EMAIL. Once out of test mode, verify a real sender domain is configured.
seed_data_creation: Inserted ord_ta_email1 order + tx_ta_email1 paxity_transactions doc; both deleted by fixture teardown after the run (verified None in Mongo post-test).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The pytest run reports 1 FAILED in iter12_email.xml, but this was a *test-side* grep regex bug (unescaped brackets in '[Email]') — the actual product behaviour was correct: exactly one email log line was produced (verified with grep -F outside pytest) and the idempotence test in the same run passed by reading confirmation_email_sent=true from Mongo. The test file has been fixed (grep -cF) for future runs. IMPORTANT: rerunning test_email_webhook.py will trigger ANOTHER real email to the merchant — only rerun when necessary.
